beats.text: Netflix paid out $1 million for a better recommendation engine.
beats.note: FlowingData says the target was an improvement of at least ten percent, and that BellKor, a statistics team at AT&T Labs, reached it in 2009.

beats.context: FlowingData says the grand prize winning solution contained over 800 models from 4 teams.

beats.text: Netflix did not ship the winning blend.
beats.note: FlowingData says algorithms from the first year of the competition were indeed used. Techdirt quotes Netflix naming two: matrix factorization and Restricted Boltzmann Machines.

beats.text: The extra accuracy was not worth the engineering.
beats.note: Netflix said the additional accuracy gains it measured did not seem to justify the engineering effort needed to bring them into production, as quoted by Techdirt.

beats.name: Instant streaming
beats.role: Launched one year after the prize began, according to Techdirt. Members now wanted something great to watch right now.

beats.text: The prize was won. The product had already moved on.
